welcome.title: Welcome to the New Setup
welcome.excerpt: Separating my professional work from my personal interests was a necessary step. Here's why I decided to build a dual-mode website.
welcome.p1: For the longest time, I tried to cram everything into one digital identity. My professional work as an EDI Integration Architect requires a certain level of precision, technical depth, and frankly, a bit of a serious face.
welcome.p2: But that's not all of who I am. I have interests in lifestyle, technology trends, and social media that don't always fit into a 'Developer Portal' aesthetic.
welcome.p3: So, I decided to split the difference. Or rather, split the site.
welcome.p4: Mode 1: Professional remains my digital CV and technical documentation hub. It's dark, monospaced, and focused on code.
welcome.p5: Mode 2: Personal (where you are right now) is for everything else. It's light, readable, and open to broader topics.
welcome.p6: Feel free to toggle between them using the button in the navigation bar. I hope this gives you a better picture of the whole person behind the code.

moments.title: Moments That Matter
moments.subtitle: Reflections on friendship, travel dreams, and finding balance
moments.excerpt: Reflections on friendship, travel dreams, and finding balance in a fast-paced world.
moments.p1: There's something liberating about stepping away from the screens and lines of code. As someone who spends most of my days architecting complex systems and debugging integration flows, I've learned that the best moments often happen when you're not optimizing anything at all.
moments.p3: I came across this beautiful world map installation recently, and it reminded me of something important: there's a whole world outside our daily routines. Each continent, each country has its own stories, cultures, and experiences waiting to be discovered.
moments.p4: As much as I love solving technical problems and building digital bridges between systems, I never want to lose sight of the physical bridges I want to cross – the places I want to explore, the diverse perspectives I want to understand.
moments.p5: Travel isn't just about the destinations. It's about stepping outside your comfort zone, challenging your assumptions, and returning home with a broader view of the world.
moments.p6: In a career that often feels like solving endless puzzles, having people who ground you is essential. These are the friends who don't care about your latest deployment or the API you just optimized. They care about you.
moments.p7: The holiday season always brings this into focus for me. The lights, the gatherings, the shared laughter – they remind me that connection is what makes everything else worthwhile.
moments.p8: Whether we're celebrating small wins or just hanging out over coffee, these moments with friends recharge me in ways that no weekend ever could.
moments.p9: I used to think 'work-life balance' was about dividing your time equally between work and everything else. But I've realized it's more nuanced than that.
moments.p10: It's about being intentional. When I'm working on an integration project, I'm fully present, solving problems and pushing systems to their limits. But when I'm with friends, exploring new places, or simply unwinding at a café, I'm equally present in those moments.
moments.p11: The key isn't splitting time 50/50. It's about ensuring that when you're living your life outside of work, you're actually living it – not mentally debugging code or planning your next sprint.
moments.p12: As we close out this year, I'm reflecting on what really matters. Yes, I'm proud of the technical challenges I've overcome and the systems I've built. But I'm equally proud of the friendships I've maintained, the experiences I've created, and the balance I'm still figuring out.
moments.p13: Here's to more spontaneous moments, more travel plans turning into actual trips, and more time with the people who make it all worthwhile.
moments.p14: Because at the end of the day, you're not measured by the number of APIs you've integrated or the bugs you've fixed. You're measured by the moments you've lived and the connections you've made.

stone.title: Stone & Shore
stone.subtitle: Ordu, İstanbul, Sümela — and a quiet motto
stone.excerpt: Temet nosce between Ordu shores, Istanbul nights, and Sumela stone.
stone.p1: Temet nosce. Know yourself. It sounds heavy until you say it on a road that already knows you — Black Sea wind in Ordu, a late table with friends, the kind of night that does not ask for a status update.
stone.p2: I keep that line close because the day job is all maps and messages: EDI lanes, APIs, systems that must agree. Off the clock, the map is simpler. Shore. Stone. People who stay.
stone.h2a: Ordu — the shore that resets the clock
stone.p3: Ordu is not a postcard I perform for. It is breakfast with a view, a bench that faces the water, twilight when the day softens. When the coast is quiet, I remember I am allowed to be quiet too.
stone.p4: Friends here do not need the résumé version of me. Fist bumps after a night drive. Rain ponchos at a waterfall. A table that fills itself. That is the proof I trust.
stone.h2b: İstanbul — the city on the water
stone.p5: İstanbul moves faster. Kız Kulesi sits in the current like a comma — a pause you notice only if you look. I like nights that keep a little noise and a little iced filtre, when the city feels close but not crowded inside your head.
stone.p6: Not every frame needs a caption. Some are just proof that I showed up for the hour.
stone.p7: Sümela Monastery does not rush you. Fresco color on cliff stone. A dome that asks you to look up. Walking through with friends turns history into company — not a lecture, a shared silence with walls that have seen more winters than we will.
stone.p8: Stone that remembers is a good mirror. You leave lighter if you let it.
stone.p9: This notebook is not a sprint board. It is the same energy as the stories: short when it can be, longer when a place deserves room. Ordu shores. İstanbul nights. Sümela stone. Temet nosce on the way.
stone.p10: The road is long, but beautiful. I will keep using this place as a notebook — not too much, just enough.

aboutMe.title: A Little About Me
aboutMe.excerpt: Curiosity, balance, and a small corner of the internet for places and moments worth keeping.
aboutMe.p1: I'm someone who enjoys discovering new things, exploring different perspectives, and figuring out how the world works.
aboutMe.p2: I appreciate a good balance between ambition and enjoying the moment. I like having goals to work toward, but I also believe that life is about the experiences, people, and little moments we collect along the way.
aboutMe.p3: I'm drawn to things that spark curiosity, whether it's a new place, an interesting idea, a great conversation, or something I've never tried before.
aboutMe.p4: This is my little corner of the internet — a place to share some of the things I enjoy, the places I discover, and the moments worth remembering.

thingsIEnjoy.title: Things I Enjoy
thingsIEnjoy.excerpt: Ordinary days made a little less ordinary — drives, design, curiosity, and joy without a productivity tax.
thingsIEnjoy.p1: I'm a fan of experiences that make ordinary days feel a little less ordinary.
thingsIEnjoy.p2: A good drive, discovering a new place, a late-night conversation, exploring something unfamiliar, or simply taking some time to clear my mind — sometimes, the simplest things are the most enjoyable.
thingsIEnjoy.p3: I also appreciate good design, technology, cars, and anything that reflects creativity and attention to detail.
thingsIEnjoy.p4: I don't think every interest needs to become a passion or every moment needs to be productive. Sometimes, enjoying something just because it makes you happy is more than enough.

evening.title: My Kind of Evening
evening.excerpt: Quieter hours, city lights, and evenings that don't need a plan.
evening.p1: There's something special about the quieter hours of the day.
evening.p2: When the noise settles down, the city lights come on, and there's finally room to slow down and enjoy your own company.
evening.p3: Sometimes it's a good playlist, sometimes a drive, sometimes an interesting conversation that lasts longer than expected.
evening.p4: I like the idea that not every evening needs a plan. Some of the best moments happen spontaneously, without expectations or a schedule.
evening.p5: For me, a good evening is less about where I am and more about how it feels to be there.

places.title: Places I Want to See
places.excerpt: Travel as atmosphere — coastlines, architecture, scenic roads, and everyday life from another angle.
places.p1: For me, traveling is about more than visiting famous landmarks. It's about experiencing a different atmosphere, discovering local places, trying new food, and seeing everyday life from another perspective.
places.p2: I'd love to explore cities with distinctive architecture, beautiful coastlines, scenic roads, and places where you can get lost for a while without worrying about the time.
places.p3: Some trips are about adventure. Others are about slowing down and enjoying the surroundings.
places.p4: My travel list is always evolving, and I hope to keep adding new destinations, unexpected discoveries, and stories worth telling.

cars.title: A Soft Spot for Cars
cars.excerpt: Design, dynamics, and the details that make an ordinary drive feel like a journey.
cars.p1: I've always found cars interesting for more than just getting from one place to another.
cars.p2: Design, proportions, driving dynamics, technology, and the character of a vehicle all make a difference. Some cars stand out because of their performance, others because of their presence on the road.
cars.p3: For me, the appeal is in the details — the way a car looks, feels, and makes an ordinary drive a little more enjoyable.
cars.p4: I enjoy comparing different models, discovering new designs, and thinking about what makes a car truly worth owning.
cars.p5: Because sometimes, the journey deserves just as much attention as the destination.

philosophy.title: Know thyself
philosophy.p1: Temet nosce is Latin for “know thyself” — ancient Delphic wisdom once carved at Apollo’s temple in Delphi.
philosophy.p2: It is a reminder to look inward before chasing the road ahead: stay honest about who you are, what you need, and what you leave behind.
philosophy.p3: For me it is less a slogan than a quiet compass — on Ordu shores, Istanbul nights, Sumela stone, and every stretch in between.
